item.title: Iran War Live Updates: Trump Claims Progress in Talks and Extends Strait of Hormuz Deadline
item.summary: President Trump has threatened to attack Iran’s power plants unless it fully reopens the Strait of Hormuz, a vital oil route, by April 6. Israel on Friday launched more strikes on Iran.

item.title: UAE and Qatar Arrest Hundreds Over Online Videos of Iranian Attacks
item.summary: The authorities have made a wave of arrests to stop people posting footage of strikes, citing security risks. Experts also see a fear of damage to the countries’ image as safe havens.

item.title: Europeans Are Angry at Trump, but Often Forgiving of Americans
item.summary: A generation ago, foreign fury over the Iraq invasion often blurred into anti-Americanism. Now, some Europeans seem ready to distinguish between the president and the American people.

item.title: Australia Temporarily Blocks Iranians With Visitor Visas From Entry
item.summary: Iranian tourists with visas will be barred for six months in case they are ‘unable or unlikely’ to go back because of the war, Australian officials said.

item.title: Rubio Expected to Press Allies Over Strait of Hormuz at G7 Meeting
item.summary: The meeting in France is slated to discuss efforts to stop the war in the Middle East, end Iran’s nuclear and ballistic missile development, and reopen maritime trade routes.

item.title: Resurgent Inflation Tests Faith in Fed’s Willingness to Tame It
item.summary: The war in the Middle East risks worsening an inflation problem that the Federal Reserve has struggled for years to subdue.

item.title: Here’s What Happened in the War in the Middle East on Thursday
item.summary: For a second time, President Trump extended the deadline for Iran to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: The German Military Tightens Its Social Media Rules
item.summary: Military members sharing clips on Instagram and TikTok have helped recruit badly needed new soldiers, but Bundeswehr officials said they are concerned about security.

item.title: The Faroe Islands, Wary After Greenland, Vote for Change
item.summary: Statehood had been a key issue in this tiny Danish archipelago before President Trump threatened Greenland. Now, Faroese voters are focused more on their own economy than geopolitics.

item.title: U.S. May Label Brazilian Gangs as Terror Groups, After Push by the Bolsonaros
item.summary: The Trump administration is weighing declaring Brazil’s two largest drug gangs terrorist groups, after lobbying by the sons of jailed former President Jair Bolsonaro.
